01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: A laptop and a printer share one Ethernet cable, speaking IP, with nothing else attached. What is it?
options: A network, but not part of the Internet — nothing joins it to another network
Not a network — there's no router

01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: What makes something "the Internet"?
options: A single owner managing all routers
Many independently owned networks joined at their boundaries by routers

01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: Which three things does a protocol define?
options: Format and order of messages, and actions taken on send/receive

01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: A server parses an HTTP request correctly and then sends nothing back. Has it followed the protocol?
options: No — the required response (action) is part of the protocol
Only if the request was GET

01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: Which device forwards on MAC addresses within one network?
Which device forwards on IP addresses between different networks?
What does a modem change?
Why does cable Internet slow at 8 pm while a DSL line doesn't?
options: Cable is one shared coaxial run for the street; DSL is a dedicated pair per home
Cable has a lower peak rate

01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: Which hop usually sets the bottleneck on a home user's path?
Forwarding is ____; routing is ____.
options: global and rare; local and per-packet
local, per-packet, microseconds; global, seconds to minutes
done by switches; done by hosts

01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: What does store-and-forward mean for a packet crossing three links?
options: It pays a full transmission delay on every link
It skips transmission on fast links

01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: 3 pkt/s arrive at a link that can send 1 pkt/s. What happens?
options: The buffer fills and about two thirds of arrivals are dropped

01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: TDM gives each user…
options: Its own frequency band all the time
The whole link for a repeating slice of time
A share only when the queue is empty

01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: A 1 Mb/s link with 100 kb/s users active 10% of the time. Circuit switching supports 10 users. Packet switching supports about…
Why is there an ISP hierarchy instead of a full mesh?
options: N networks need N(N−1)/2 links — impossible to build and pay for
Routers can only have two ports

01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: Two access ISPs that both buy transit from the same tier-1 start peering at a local IXP. What changes?
options: They no longer need the tier-1 at all
Traffic between their customers stops crossing the tier-1 and paying transit; they still need it for everything else

01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: Which delay does NOT depend on packet length or link rate?
Which of the four nodal delays is the only one that changes with load?
A tenfold faster link on a long path (London → Thunder Bay) cuts total one-way delay by only ~2%. Why?
options: Propagation dominates, and a faster link doesn't change it

01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: Traffic intensity goes above 1. What does a bigger buffer do?
options: Converts loss into latency — it doesn't fix I > 1

01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: A path has links of 100, 1 and 100 Mb/s. What is the throughput?
What does a link-layer switch read from an arriving frame?
In the five-layer stack, the transport layer's unit is a…
01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.explain: Application: message · Transport: segment · Network: datagram · Link: frame · Physical: bits.

01-computer-networks-and-the-internet.q: What does encapsulation mean?
options: Each layer opens and modifies the one above
Each layer wraps what it's given without opening it; the receiver unwraps in reverse order

01-equation-sheet.q: What is L for a 1,500-byte packet?
01-equation-sheet.explain: Bytes × 8. The missing factor of eight is the commonest lost mark.

01-equation-sheet.q: Transmission delay of a 1,000-byte packet on a 2 Mb/s link?
Propagation delay over 1,000 km of fiber (s = 2×10⁸ m/s)?
01-equation-sheet.explain: 10⁶ / 2×10⁸ = 5 ms. Rule of thumb: fiber covers 200 km per ms.

01-equation-sheet.q: A 1,500-byte packet joins a 10 Mb/s queue behind 3 packets of the same size. Queueing delay?
1,000-byte packet, 400 km, 2 Mb/s, 2 packets queued, negligible processing. Nodal delay?
01-equation-sheet.explain: L/R = 4 ms. Queue 8 + trans 4 + prop 2 = 14 ms.

01-equation-sheet.q: A 1,500-byte packet crosses three idle 10 Mb/s links. Ignoring propagation, what is the total transmission delay?
L = 12,000 bits, a = 500 pkt/s, R = 10 Mb/s. Traffic intensity I?
A 20-slot buffer on a link where L/R = 1.2 ms. What's the longest possible queueing wait?
A 10 MB file crosses a path of 20, 5 and 100 Mb/s links. Download time?
01-equation-sheet.explain: F = 80×10⁶ bits. Throughput = min = 5 Mb/s. T = 16 s.

01-equation-sheet.q: 4 MB file, server uploads at 2 Mb/s, your access link is 1 Mb/s. Which change halves the download time?
01-equation-sheet.explain: The bottleneck is your 1 Mb/s access link: 32 s → 16 s.

01-equation-sheet.q: A 2 Mb/s link divided into 250 kb/s TDM slots supports how many users?

02-equation-sheet.q: Non-persistent HTTP: 1 HTML + 5 objects, RTT 50 ms, negligible transmission. Total time?
How much does persistent HTTP save over non-persistent for n referenced objects?
02-equation-sheet.explain: Exactly the n skipped connection setups.

02-equation-sheet.q: 10 req/s of 100 kbit objects over a 2 Mb/s access link, no cache. Utilization ρ?
Same link with a 50% cache hit rate. ρ?
Why can a bigger access link never beat a cache on average response time?
options: A bigger link lowers ρ but never removes the RTT to the origin; a cache removes it for every hit
It can always beat a cache

02-equation-sheet.q: u_s = 5u, F/u = 1 h, N = 20. Client–server distribution time (ignore download limits)?
Same setup with P2P where each peer uploads u. Distribution time?
02-equation-sheet.explain: Largest of F/u_s = 0.2 h and NF/(u_s + Σu_i) = 20/25 = 0.8 h.

02-equation-sheet.q: How does client–server distribution time grow with N, compared to P2P?
options: Client–server grows linearly; P2P flattens toward F/u

02-equation-sheet.q: Raw rate of 1280 × 720 video at 24 bits/pixel and 30 fps?
A player has received 40 s of video and played 25 s. How much is buffered?
A record with TTL 6 h is cached at 10 a.m. and changed at 11 a.m. Until when can users see the old answer?
02-equation-sheet.explain: Stale until t_cached + TTL = 10 a.m. + 6 h, not t_changed + TTL.

02-the-application-layer.q: What actually communicates across the network?
A socket is…
options: A physical port on a router
The API between an application process and the transport layer

02-the-application-layer.q: What does a port number do?
options: Gets the message to the right machine
Gets the message to the right process on that machine

02-the-application-layer.q: Which transport requirement can NO protocol buy you?
02-the-application-layer.explain: Timing and guaranteed throughput can't be bought; integrity is paid for by resending.

02-the-application-layer.q: A multiplayer game sends positions 30×/s and a late position is useless. TCP or UDP?
options: UDP — retransmission would deliver something obsolete

02-the-application-layer.q: Why does DNS use UDP?
options: The exchange (2 messages) is shorter than a TCP handshake + teardown (9)

02-the-application-layer.q: What is TLS?
options: A library the application adds on top of a reliable connection for encryption, integrity and authentication

02-the-application-layer.q: HTTP being stateless is what…
options: Let the Web scale — any machine behind a name can answer — and why carts need cookies

02-the-application-layer.q: RTT includes which of these?
options: Propagation both ways plus queueing and processing

02-the-application-layer.q: Why did HTTP/3 move to UDP via QUIC?
options: With TCP, one lost packet stalls every HTTP/2 stream; QUIC does reliability per stream

02-the-application-layer.q: Which header has been mandatory in requests since HTTP/1.1, enabling virtual hosting?
A hand-typed request is sent but the server never replies. Most likely cause?
options: The blank line ending the headers was never sent

02-the-application-layer.q: A 5xx status means…
options: You asked correctly and the server broke

02-the-application-layer.q: You delete a shop's cookie from your browser. What happens to their database record about you?
options: Nothing — you threw away your key, not their record

02-the-application-layer.q: Which cookie flag stops scripts from reading the session cookie?
02-the-application-layer.explain: Secure: encrypted connections only. SameSite=Lax: defends against CSRF.

02-the-application-layer.q: How does a third-party ad network track you across sites?
options: Via an embedded object (e.g. a 1×1 pixel) — each fetch carries its own cookie plus a Referer

02-the-application-layer.q: In an iterated DNS query, who does all the asking?
Why is iterated resolution used instead of recursive?
options: Recursive is slower for the host
In recursive resolution the root ends up doing the most work

02-the-application-layer.q: With an empty cache, an iterated lookup of gaia.cs.umass.edu: how many queries does the resolver send, and which reply has the address?
"DNS changes take 24–48 h to propagate." What's really happening?
options: Records are copied server to server
Nothing propagates — records are live instantly; old cached copies take time to expire

02-the-application-layer.q: Which record type returns an address and ends the search?
What ties a DNS reply to its question, and why is it a weakness?
options: The TCP connection; it can't be forged
A 2-byte identification field over UDP — guess it and answer first, and you poison the cache

02-the-application-layer.q: What does DNSSEC do?
options: Signs records so forged answers fail — authenticates but doesn't hide, and doesn't stop flooding

02-the-application-layer.q: Why does email need two protocols where the Web needed one?
options: The recipient isn't there when mail arrives — SMTP pushes to an always-on server, IMAP/POP pulls later

02-the-application-layer.q: A message arrives with From: accounts@bank.example. What did the receiving server verify?
options: Nothing — it delivers on the envelope (MAIL FROM / RCPT TO) and never reads From:
The sender's IP is a bank

02-the-application-layer.q: You mark a message unread on your phone and your laptop shows it too. Which protocol?
A conditional GET with an unchanged object returns 304. What does it save?
options: Bandwidth — the round trip is still paid

02-the-application-layer.q: Why does BitTorrent cut files into pieces?
options: So peers have different things to trade and can upload within ~30 s of arriving

02-the-application-layer.q: What is the optimistic unchoke for?
options: Giving a new peer with nothing a chance to show it will upload, and finding better partners

02-the-application-layer.q: In DASH, who decides which quality to fetch next?
How does a CDN steer you to a nearby cluster?
options: DNS: a CNAME into the CDN, whose name server picks a cluster based on the resolver's location

02-the-application-layer.q: A UDP server can't reply to the client. What did it most likely discard?
options: The sender address returned by recvfrom

02-the-application-layer.q: A TCP server closes the socket accept() returned. What happens to the next client?
options: It connects normally — the welcoming socket is still listening

final.q: Host A sends to B on the same home network, then to a server in Toronto. Which device handles each?
options: Switch for the first (MAC); router for the second (IP)

final.q: Host is a role, not a size. Which of these is a host?
A data center uses a leaf-spine mesh. If one spine fails, what happens?
In an enterprise tree with one border router, the border router fails. What happens?
In FDM, user 3 goes silent. What happens to their band?
Packet switching's price for supporting more users than circuit switching is…
In the ISP hierarchy, money flows ____ and routes flow ____.
Tier-1 ISPs…
options: Have global reach, buy transit from nobody, and peer settlement-free with each other

final.q: Doubling the packet size changes which delay?
Moving the receiver farther away changes which delay?
A 1,500-byte packet on a 100 Mb/s link over 1,000 km of fiber, idle. One-way delay?
1,500-byte packet: link 1 at 100 Mb/s (1 ms prop), link 2 at 10 Mb/s (5 ms prop), link 3 at 50 Mb/s (2 ms prop). End-to-end delay?
Traffic intensity approaches 1. What happens to queueing delay?
You upgrade a link that isn't the bottleneck. Throughput…
Which device reads up to the network layer?
The end-to-end principle says…
options: Every router must open transport headers
Nothing in the middle opens the transport header — so layers above the link can change without touching switches
All traffic goes through a tier-1

final.q: Why can a brand new application (like the Web once was) be deployed without permission from network operators?
options: Application code only runs at the edge; routers carry messages but never run your code

final.q: A bank transfer and a voice call have different needs. Which does the voice call tolerate?
Which protocols run over TCP?
12 kB HTML + 10 × 60 kB images, 10 Mb/s, RTT 100 ms. Non-persistent ≈ 2.69 s, persistent ≈ 1.69 s. What dominates the slower time?
HTTP/1.1's remaining problem that HTTP/2 addressed was…
options: Responses must return in order, so a slow one blocks those behind it

final.q: Which HTTP method is idempotent and stores the payload at exactly the given path?
After login, what is the credential for the rest of the session?
A signed token in the cookie instead of a server-side session table makes what hard?
options: Early logout — the token stays valid until it expires

final.q: Which of these is NOT a reason DNS isn't one central database?
options: Every query on Earth at one door

final.q: A DNS flood against the root mostly fails. Why?
options: Resolvers already cache TLD delegations, so caching is the defense

final.q: When you register networkutopia.com, which records does the registrar write into the .com TLD server?
options: An NS record and an A record for your name server

final.q: In SMTP, who speaks first?
Why are email attachments larger than the original file?
options: SMTP was historically 7-bit text, so binary is encoded into printable characters

final.q: Why can't email simply forbid forged From: lines?
options: The same envelope/letter split that allows forgery also makes forwarding and mailing lists work

final.q: A web cache acts as a ____ to the browser and a ____ to the origin on a miss.
Why does BitTorrent request the rarest piece first?
options: Insurance — a piece down to one holder vanishes when that peer leaves

final.q: Why does a player buffer video before starting?
options: To absorb uneven network delivery so playback doesn't stall

final.q: Why does DASH pass through firewalls and proxies that blocked 1990s streaming protocols?
options: It's ordinary HTTP over TCP fetching stored files

final.q: Akamai's "enter deep" strategy buys ____ at the cost of ____.
options: the shortest path to users; thousands of sites in networks it doesn't own

final.q: A user's DNS resolver is in another country, and the CDN serves them from there. Why?
options: The CDN sees the resolver's location, not the user's

final.q: A TCP server uses a welcoming socket. What does accept() return?
options: A second, dedicated socket for this client

final.q: With a UDP socket, where is the destination address written?
